Per: Justice Vivek Rusia 1.

The petitioner has filed this present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief(s):-
"(i) To direct, the respondents to make the payment of compensation along with interest at the rate of 15% per annum under Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 as the amount has not been paid within the period of one year.
(ii) To direct alternatively that the respondents decide pending representations of the petitioner within the time frame as fixed by this Hon'ble Court, preferably within the Smt Bharti Vaghela vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68124128/
1 period of one month.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28598 -2- (iii) To grant any other just, suitable and proper relief, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit, may also kindly be granted to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Costs be also awarded in favour of the petitioner.

(iv) To pass any other writ/order/direction which this Hon'ble Court deems fit in light of the facts and circumstances of the case along with an order as to costs of the petition."
2.

The petitioner has been an owner of the land bearing Survey No.1006/1/1/2 admeasuring 1.478 hectare, Survey No.1003 admeasuring 1.171 hectares and Survey No.1002/1/2/1 admeasuring 1.012 hectare, total 3.661 hectares situated in village Simrol, Tehsil Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, Mhow, District Indore (M.P.).
3.
Out of the aforesaid land of the petitioner, the National Highway Authority had acquired 0.824 hectare of the land for construction of National Highway 347 BG Indore-Edlabad Highway.
The petitioner had been paid the compensation of Rs.96,29,043/- for the aforesaid land after the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
These facts are not in dispute between the parties.
According to the petitioner, while constructing the highway, 0.442 hectare of the additional land has been illegally taken by the respondents without acquisition and compensation.
The petitioner submitted a representation to the respondent No.4 on 14.2.2023 for grant of compensation for additional 0.442 hectare land and the damage to the adjoining land.

4. The respondent No.4 vide letter dated 9.3.2023 directed the Upper Tehsildar, Tappa Simrol,
Tehsil Mhow to submit a report within 7 days.
On 28.7.2023 the spot inspection was carried out.

After the spot inspection, the Additional Tehsildar has submitted a report to the CALA / SDO that the area of acquired land of the petitioner is 0.366 hectare but on the spot additional NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28598 -3- land of 0.458 hectare has also been taken by the NHAI.
It is also reported that on the spot, one well on the land has also been affected due to acquisition.
Thereafter the petitioner sent a legal notice to the National Highway Authority for payment of additional compensation, but no reply was given.
Hence, the petitioner has approached this Court by way of writ petition.
5. In the reply, the respondents have given the history of acquisition of the land and passing of the award by CALA which is not in dispute.
Neither para-wise reply has been given, nor there has been specific denial of allegation of acquisition of extra land without payment of compensation.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. Vide order dated 17.9.2025 the respondents No.4 & 5 were directed to visit the spot and take measurement of the land in dispute and submit a report before this Court.

In compliance of the aforesaid order, the Sub Divisional Officer, Khudel and Dr. Ambedkar Nagar jointly visited the spot and drawn a Panchnama, which is reproduced below:-

7. As per the aforesaid Panchnama, the land of the petitioner bearing Survey No.1006/1/1/2 area 0.305 hectare and Survey No.1002/1/2/1 area 0.153 hectare has been used for construction of tunnel and road and no compensation has been paid.

Along with the aforesaid report, a colored map mentioning the exact location and area has also been brought on record, which is reproduced below:-
8.
The land acquisition proceedings initiated vide Notification No.729(E) dated 5.2.2019 had come to an end by passing the final award dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28598 -5- 16.3.2021.
After disbursement of the compensation and taking the possession of the land, the CALA becomes functus officio.

Therefore, now the NHAI has two options; (i) either to initiate fresh proceedings for acquisition of the land bearing Survey No.1006/1/1/2 area 0.305 hectare and Survey No.1002/1/2/1 area 0.153 hectare, in accordance with law or (ii) pay the compensation at the same rate as determined by the CALA for payment of compensation of the land of the petitioner i.e.
Survey No.1006/1/1/1 Area 0.350 hectare & Survey No.1002/1/2/1 area 0.016 hectare along with the interest.

9. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner fairly submits that the petitioner is ready to accept the compensation at the same rate on which the compensation for the earlier acquired land was paid.
Mr Bhatijiwale has not opposed the same.

10. Therefore, upon payment of compensation of the land with interest, the land bearing Survey No.1006/1/1/2 area 0.305 hectare and Survey No.1002/1/2/1 area 0.153 hectare shall be treated as acquired by the respondents No.1 & 2.
Let the amount be calculated and payment be made within a period of 60 days from today, failing which the same shall carry interest @ 12% per annum after expiry of 60 days till payment.
